primary_sources.claim_used: Seregin Theorem 3.1 produces a nontrivial ancient Euler limit with scale-weighted energy/pressure/gradient control and local energy inequality.
Abe constructs classical axisymmetric traveling-wave Euler vortex rings; the moving-frame velocity vanishes at spatial infinity and vorticity is compactly supported.
Cao et al. treat global steady vortex rings as traveling-wave Euler solutions with kinetic-energy/impulse variational structure.

derived_check.statement: For c != 0 and h >= 0 in L1(R^3), integral_{-a^2}^0 integral_{B(a)} h(x+c*tau) dx d tau <= (2a/|c|)||h||_1.

result: Centered backward local smallness plus the displayed F=1 local/spacetime budget is not by itself a faithful global-triviality surrogate under noncompact translation; an exact no-incoming-energy/tightness/recentering bridge remains necessary.
scope_boundary: No specific cited vortex ring is claimed to satisfy every exact global integrability/local-energy hypothesis of Seregin Theorem 3.1; that stronger counterexample claim remains open.
cross_lane_pattern: locally meaningful surrogate/local result != root-critical quantity until a separate preservation/gluing interface is proved
